newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Peregrine to seek more debt ratings.
newsitem.headline: Peregrine to seek more debt ratings.

text.p: Asian investment bank Peregrine Investments Holdings Ltd said on Thursday it intended to seek debt ratings from international rating agencies Standard & Poor's and Moody's Investors Service this year.
Japan Bond Research Institute on Thursday assigned a BBB+ rating to the group's unsecured long-term debt.

Peregrine chairman Philip Tose told a news conference the rating would increase the firm's funding capacity in Japan, and it intended to tap the Japanese financial market for funds, possibly by issuing bonds.
But he added the group had no immediate plan to do so.
Peregrine had increasing capital needs due to the changing nature of its business, Tose said.

"Pure (securities) agency business is becoming a very thin-margin business and the whole area of derivatives, structural trade is going to play a bigger and bigger role as we go forward, which requires bigger and bigger capital," he said.
The group was likely to liquidate two to three direct investments this year although the timing would depend on the market, he said.
Peregrine's direct investment business, which had not performed very well, would pick up "quite significantly" in 1998 and beyond, Tose said.
The group's turnover in 1996 was expected to be more than double the HK$84.39 billion in 1995, he said.
"I haven't actually seen the final figure but it will be more than double the 1995 figure," he said, adding he expected further significant growth in 1997.
Peregrine recorded turnover of HK$77.66 million for the six months to June 30, 1996, versus HK$31.43 million a year earlier.
Tose said he was very satified with the group's results regarding equity products last year, even though the Asian equity markets had been tougher in 1996 in general.
Peregrine raised a total of about US$2.6 billion for Asian corporates last year, he said.
The firm would benefit from an expected flurry of fund raising in the first half of this year when the equity markets in the region would improve on last year, Tose added.

"I think we will see substantial fund raising in the first half of this year. I think that's only natural. But I believe there is the appetite for it. So we remain quite optimistic on that front. We certanly as a group have a very full calendar of issues not just in Hong Kong but throughout Asia," he said.
The group's fixed income business would continue to expand in areas that it was already involved in, he said.

"It will continue to broaden its base of business. They are becoming more active in places like the domestic markets in Korea, in India and elsewhere in the region and we believe that activity in the overall fixed income business is going to increase along the same line as we have seen in the last couple of years."
